newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Japan must formally compensate sex slaves - Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Japan must formally compensate sex slaves - Seoul.

text.p: South Korea on Wednesday urged Tokyo to halt private compensation for Korean women forced to work as sex slaves by Japanese Imperial Army soldiers during World War Two, the foreign ministry said.
"We want such compensation stopped immediately," a spokesman quoted Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha as telling his visiting Japanese counterpart Yukihiko Ikeda during a meeting.
"It is regretable that a private-sector fund secretly paid compensation to a handful of comfort women," he added.
"The compensation should be made at the government level," Yoo was quoted as saying.
The ministry reported this week that the Asian Women's Fund, a private group set up in 1995 with Japanese initiative, paid two million yen ($17,100) in compensation to five Korean women.
Ikeda is visiting Seoul to discuss preparations for President Kim Young-sam's January 25-26 visit to Japan.

The spokesman said President Kim was expected to discuss with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto the issue of cooperation on North Korea, co-hosting of the 2002 World Cup soccer tournament and trade and investment ties during his visit.
